content:
Carlos's initial cost to plant the tree is $90.  
Each year, he harvests 7 lemons and sells them for $1.50 each, giving an annual revenue of \(7 \times 1.5 = \$10.50\).  
The annual cost to water and feed the tree is $3.  
So, the net annual profit is \(10.50 - 3 = \$7.50\).

To find out when he starts earning money overall, we need the cumulative net profit to exceed the initial $90 cost.  
The break-even point is when total net profit equals the initial cost:  
\(n \times 7.50 = 90\)  
\(n = 90 / 7.50 = 12\) years.

After 12 years, he has exactly recovered his initial investment (net profit = $0). He begins to earn money (positive overall profit) in the 13th year.

Answer: 13
